page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.2 GHz. The CPU configuration consists of 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes an L3 cache of 16 MB, an L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and an L1d cache of 32 KB. It supports hardware features such as AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1101.98, and the multi-core score is 1451.88, both falling in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 12.0 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 841.0 and a multi-core score of 1028.0. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.43 GB/sec, while LLM inference using a small 135M model achieves 133.75 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 61.66 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-2 provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core within a budget-friendly hardware class. This resource density makes it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput or local storage performance. Appropriate workloads include lightweight database operations, caching layers, basic web serving, and small-scale background utility tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
